requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the sources satisfy `requirements.references.outline_comments`.** I read the code and tests against each obligation and found no gap that needs a FIXME. The one rough edge (item 5 below) is minor.

**Implementation**

- **Profiles define comments.**
  - `Profile::is_comment` is set per language: Rust (`line_comment`/`block_comment`), Python, TOML, YAML and TypeScript/TSX via `kind_is_comment`, and CSS via `is_comment`, which adds `js_comment`.
  - Markdown's `is_comment` (`src/outline/markdown.rs`) accepts only an `html_block` that starts with `<!--` and ends with `-->`. An inline HTML comment therefore stays paragraph text of its section.
  - Every profile static carries the `{impl}` marker.
- **Runs.** `assign_comments` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) groups comments into runs. A comment joins the previous one only if all of these hold:
  - The two have the same container binding.
  - Neither follows code on its line (`trails_code`).
  - The gap between them is whitespace.
  - The next comment starts on the line after the previous one ends, or the same line.
  
  This gives "consecutive lines, no other source between" as one run. A comment that follows code, including another comment, is its own run.
- **Trailing comments.** `trailing_owner` assigns the innermost node whose pre-widening line range covers the line, and the root when none does. This matches the requirement.
- **Other runs.** `run_owner` finds the smallest node whose byte range contains the run. It returns the first child starting at or after the run's end, otherwise the container. The container is the root at top level.
- **Container binding.** The Rust profile's `comment_binds_to_container` is `is_inner_doc_comment`, covering `//!` and `/*!`. Such a run belongs to the smallest containing node, which is the root at file level. Other profiles use `never`.
- **References count for the owning node.**
  - `rust_coverage::missing_function_references` credits a reference to `comment.owner`, which carries out the `rust_item_coverage` half.
  - For `authoring_inputs`, `reference_selector` uses `owner_at_line`, which prefers the comment owner. The `references` tool and `reference_set_digest` do the same.
  - `nodes_for_lines` and `nodes_for_range` select comment owners when asked.
- **Extra behaviour.** Widening an owner's line range to cover its comments, and YAML's `trailing_comments_outside`, are not stated in this requirement. They are consistent with the outline requirements and the `selector_raw_lines` example, so I do not count them as gaps.
- **Judgment call on run splitting.** Runs split when the container binding differs, so `//! x` followed by `// y` on the next line form two runs. The requirement does not say how mixed runs resolve, and this reading is consistent with the "MAY bind a comment kind" clause.
- **Minor edge.** `owner_at_line` takes the first owner when several comments with different owners touch one line, such as `/* a */ /* {impl}… */`. This is a rare case.

**Tests** (`src/outline/tests.rs` and others)

- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` covers:
  - file-level `//!` going to the root
  - a run before a node
  - a trailing comment
  - a comment inside a function
  - a floating run going to the next node (`mod[m]`)
  - module `//!`
  - the tail of a module going to the module
  - a top-level tail going to the root
  - line-range widening
- `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next`, `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` cover single-case boundaries.
- `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` covers nested trailing cases.
- `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers a comment following another comment.
- `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` covers both `//!` and `/*! */`.
- `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` covers the Markdown profile rule.
- The YAML tests, including `workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows`, cover the grammar-specific trailing-comment case.
- The consumers are tested too:
  - `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` checks authoring inputs.
  - `search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners` checks search.
  - `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node` checks the digest.

Tests cover the main boundaries and failure cases.

profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
